newsitem.title: FRANCE: French tax reform will not help growth - poll.
newsitem.headline: French tax reform will not help growth - poll.

text.p: The French do not believe a tax reform plan announced last week by French Prime Minister Alain Juppe will boost economic growth, lift confidence or help cut unemployment, a poll published on Monday in financial daily La Tribune Desfosses showed.
The poll found that 69 percent believed the tax reform would not restore confidence to the French people and 71 percent believed it would not boost economic growth.
Fully 80 percent believed the tax plan would not help lower unemployment, the poll found.

The centerpiece of the plan was a 75 billion franc income tax cut over the next five years including 25 billion in 1997 on 1996 income. The 25 billion tax cut would be partly neutralised by a rise in taxes on savings and excise duties on tobacco, alcohol and petrol.
The poll, conducted on September 6 and 7, questioned 1,002 people and found that 42 percent believed the tax reform was a good thing compared to 39 percent who thought it was a bad idea.
